processing: The exact steps are little documented. As a fine Hanzhong green, it is fixed with heat, shaped into a slim eyebrow form and dried, as is typical of its class.
harvest_season: Dates are little documented. As with other Hanzhong greens, spring tea is the prized picking.
appearance_dry: Even, slender, eyebrow-like strands, tender green with visible down.
taste_profile: A tender aroma that lasts, with a fresh, mellow taste.

brewing.notes: A slim, tender green, so cool the water first. A tall glass shows the leaf well.

vintage_note: Like other Chinese greens it is usually sold as the current spring's harvest and is best drunk within about a year. It comes under the wider Hanzhong Xianhao regional family, so a pack may carry both names. Dingjun and Dingjun Mingmei are also registered trademarks, so this is partly a brand as well as a style.
description:
Dingjun Mingmei is a green tea from Mian county in Hanzhong, southern Shaanxi, named after Dingjun Mountain, the old battlefield nearby. Mingmei means tea eyebrow, which describes the slender leaf.

The main growing area is the Xiaohemiao and Dashuya hills west of Hanzhong, with gardens at about 800 to 1,380 metres near the upper Han river, misty and with soft light. Little is published on its exact method, but it sits among the finer shaped Hanzhong greens.

The cup is yellow-green and bright, fresh and mellow, with a tender aroma that lasts. The leaf at the bottom stays whole and tender green, which is a good quality check for any tea of this kind. Use cooled water and do not over-steep.

It is one of the named teas in the Hanzhong Xianhao family. As the name is also a trademark, look for the maker and the harvest date.
history:
The modern tea dates from Mian county's push to develop tea from the 1980s on. It passed a ministry-level appraisal in Hangzhou in August 1990 and went on to win a string of prizes, including a Lu Yu Cup and a silver medal at the first China Agricultural Expo.

Regional accounts say it was chosen as a state banquet tea in 1996, a claim that comes from promotional sources. It won provincial gold awards in 1997 and 1998.
